'Dad, we are not walking out of the match. It's my first time in Old Trafford!' - An afternoon with my 10-year-old inside the Theatre of Screams for Carrick's last stand

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1448 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • ‘Mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers.
  • More than 70,000 spectators leaving their seat and walking out of the stadium in the 21st minute have been quite the statement, especially live on Sky Sports.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:49 EST, 14 November 2026.

THE guy with the flyer was persistent.

‘Mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’ he asks earnestly, handing me a leaflet that unveils: ‘Enough is Enough! Empty Old Trafford! Leave the stadium in the 21st minute. 21 years of failed ownership. Glazers OUT! Ineos OUT!’.

More than 70,000 spectators leaving their seat and walking out of the stadium in the 21st minute have been quite the statement, especially live on Sky Sports.

But as admirable as Saeed TV’s aim is (I discover later he is some sort of youtuber), it’s hard to see gain any traction.

‘Dad, we are not walking out of the match. It’s my first time in Old Trafford,’ I am told as we continue to meander up Matt Busby Way, a declaration from my 10-year-old that causes a fair bit of mirth among the crowd.

In a recent development, mate, we are walking out in the 21st minute to protest 21 years of the Glazers. Will you join us?’.

‘What’s wrong with the owners anyway?’ Dan enquires innocently, which leads to a bind.

How deep down the rabbit-hole should I go with my ten-year-old on his first visit to the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s probably not the time or place to try and explain leveraged buyouts and how much debt the Glazers have saddled the club with, £1.2 billion at the last count while taking millions out of it in dividends. Do I need to go further back and talk about Rock of Gibraltar’s unexpected success on the track and the concept of stud fees?

‘They are not putting enough money into the team and taking loads of money out of the club,’ is all I offer.

‘When Manchester City need a midfielder, they can buy Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez while United have to make do with someone who was sitting on Chelsea’s bench.’.

He doesn’t look convinced that’s much of a reason to walk out of a football but as the cathedral of consumerism that is the Manchester United megastore has appeared, he forgets about United’s disastrous ownership model – for now, at least.

During his doomed attempt to coax Jurgen Klopp to Old Trafford around 2014, Ed Woodward apparently told him that United was the sporting version of Disneyland.

And to be sardined inside the megastore in the couple of hours before kick-off, you have to accept that the much-maligned former CEO may have been right about one thing.

Sources indicate that think Arnott’s a couple of days before Christmas, just with a lot more people. You even need to pass through airport-like security before even entering and spend your dosh.

One of the common refrains among United supporters is why are the Glazers holding onto the club when they don’t even seem to care.

Thirty seconds inside the megastore on match-day and you realise why the Americans are so keen to hold onto the asset they’re bleeding dry – and they probably care a great deal.

Dan gets obligatory photo at statue of United's holy trinity, a moment he will look back on.

Even with the team languishing in the relegation zone, having won a single league game all season, people are keen to spend, spend, spend.

I see people wandering around with five or six different shirts, from different eras (I did succumb and bought Dan the black shirt from 95-96 season, because it reminds me of Eric Cantona, Roy Keane and better times!).

You can get a photo with a replica of a Premier League trophy. That’s just £10. Or Lego sets of Old Trafford or the Munich clock.

Sources indicate that that will just set you back £25. For many in this shop, it seems allowing the club to empty their wallet is as much a part of the day as the actual football.

There are other parts of the ritual, which remain and have yet to be infected by the poisonous atmosphere around the club – and remind the three dads bringing their kids to Old Trafford for the first time of better days.

Such as curry chips and battered sausage from Lou Macari’s chipper. And the customary photo in front of the statue of the holy trinity of Best, Law and Charlton.

The megastore was the one place that seemed immune to the toxicity in the air. Once outside again and all that could be heard was the moans and groans, mainly because Shea Lacey wasn’t starting.

Coming here since the 1990s, we have seen the skyline of Manchester transformed as it became a sleek, modern city. It seems the one place that hasn’t changed is Old Trafford. It has remained the same.

Sources indicate that stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium – and not just because of the leaking roof. It could do with a lick or two of paint.

Stuck in time. It looked sleek and modern in 1999, but now there is a tired, decrepit feel to the stadium.

No wonder Massive Sir Jim is determined to plough ahead with his aims to make a crudely-designed circus tent ‘the Wembley of the North.’ Not that there is anyone inside Old Trafford of the same mind.

Senne Lammens has just trotted onto the field with Tom Heaton and Karl Darlow to do their pre-match warm-up when the chants start, telling Jim Ratcliffe he can stick his newly introduced stadium up his posterior.

It is a weird atmosphere, with all the chanting against the owners – both Glazers and Ineos – and nothing being sung in support of the players.

As my friend points out it must be so difficult for the team to show the best of themselves when things are this toxic in the stadium.

Dan has been to the Jodi Stand enough times on a Friday night to know there is plenty of choice and crude language at football matches, but still I nearly felt at covering his ears at some of the stuff being sung in Old Trafford last Sunday, especially that directed at CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

We had hoped that things might have been different when the game kicked off, but within a minute, Aston Villa had scored.

And three minutes later, they had scored again when Lammens fumbled Alysson’s shot into Nicolas Jackson’s path. Maybe walking out in the 21st minute wasn’t such a bad idea.

The crowd’s ire had gone from the owners to the players now, with a sustained chant of ‘You are not fit to wear the shirt.’ United did rally and by half-time, it was 2-2. But the mood was still dismal as we queued for a quick beer.

Industry observers note that the 1958 Group had asked fans not to buy booze, another protest against the owners. But it seemed nobody was paying much attention to that.

One of the concerns at United is that there seem to be too many splintered fan groups – there is also ClaimBackUnited and Fan Coalition ’58 – as well as Saeed TV, who seemed to be on his own solo run.

We didn’t feel bad about ignoring the booze ban, as everyone was doing it. And within a couple of minutes of the second-half, we saw the reason why. You need to fortify yourself to watch Diogo Dalot try to defend.

For much of the second-half, it seemed like Michael Carrick’s brief tenure was going to peter out in a forgettable defeat, as Villa seemed to manage the game perfectly.

Dan and his friends were growing frustrated, pointing out the players weren’t doing what their coaches tell them to do on a weekly basis, leading me to conclude that maybe my son’s under-11 side are better-coached than United.

The last on-pitch act of Carrick's tenure.

Recent findings suggest that and then there was the chaotic and crazy final few minutes in stoppage-time. And a draw that came out of nowhere and was celebrated like a victory.

That was the thing. Even though the mood inside the stadium was toxic for most of the game, even though the team were two down inside four minutes and the season has been a disaster, everyone still came away from Old Trafford, happy and with a smile on their face.

Only football can do that. More than that, perhaps only Manchester United – despite everything – can do that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethan Nwaneri (19) registered two assists in England U21s recent 3-2 victory over France, but the Borussia Dortmund man has struggled for playing time in the Bundesliga recently.

Speaking at Thursday’s press conference, BVB head coach Niko Kovač weighed in on the player’s situation. “We have very good players in those positions up front, he explained. Nwaneri initially replaced Giannis Konstantelias, who suffered an ACL injury on his Bundesliga debut against Hamburg, while Fabio Silva is shining alongside Serhou Guirassy, while Konstantinos Karetsas has recently returned from a back injury.

“The competition is tough,” added Kovač, who did praise Nwaneri’s performances for England. “As far as Ethan is concerned, we’re delighted,” he said. ” It was a friendly match and he did really well.”.

With an assist to his name on his Bundesliga but against Hoffenheim on Matchday 2, Nwaneri has featured in eight of nine possible league games, playing 336 minutes for Die Schwarzgelben in Germany’s top flight.

On Saturday, Dortmund face Borussia Mönchengladbach at Borussia-Park as they look to maintain their unbeaten start to their Bundesliga campaign.

L’ex giocatore ricorda i rimproveri nello spogliatoio del Milan e gli scherzi organizzati con Pirlo.

Recent findings suggest that massimo Oddo indica in Gennaro Gattuso il principale artefice del primato della Lazio in Serie A. L’ex giocatore biancoceleste e del Milan ha parlato del rapporto con l’amico ed ex compagno di squadra in un’intervista a Repubblica. Oltre al giudizio sull’attuale allenatore della Lazio, ha ricordato il ruolo che aveva nello spogliatoio rossonero e alcuni episodi vissuti insieme.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Secondo Oddo, l’esperienza da commissario tecnico della Nazionale, conclusa senza la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha inciso sulla consapevolezza di Gattuso. Non ne avrebbe però cambiato il modo di essere: «Gattuso non cambia, migliora. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima».

Oddo riconosce nell’allenatore della Lazio un ruolo che aveva già ai tempi del Milan: «ma è sempre stato un “braccio armato” pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi. Già ai tempi del Milan. Rino rieducava senza mai punire». Il richiamo arrivava anche per piccoli ritardi e, nel suo racconto, non richiedeva l’intervento del club.

L’ex compagno precisa: «bastavano due minuti di ritardo – capitava soprattutto ai brasiliani, esclusi Dida e Kakà – e scattava il rimprovero. Non serviva l’intervento della società».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich maintained their unbeaten start to the season but had to come from behind to secure a share of the spoils against struggling Cologne with Nathaniel Brown cancelling out Mikey Moore’s first-half strike.

The massive news coming into Friday’s Matchday 10 curtain-raiser was Vincent Kompany’s return to the touchline, one month after he collapsed at the club’s training ground.

Bayern remained unchanged following their 2-1 victory against Mainz prior to the international break, but the notable inclusion on the bench was 19-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora, who was named in Bayern’s matchday squad for the first time, while Cologne made once change after their 2-1 derby defeat against Bayer Leverkusen, with Luka Lochoshvili coming into defence for attacker Marius Bülter.

In a recent development, michael Olise threatened early on for the hosts, but it was Cologne who took an early lead at the Allianz Arena. Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore opened his Bundesliga account for the season in the 12th minute, rounding Jonas Urbig and slotting into an empty net. It then went from bad to worse for Bayern when Harry Kane was forced off with what looked to be an ankle injury.

Bayern’s equaliser arrived in the 37th minute when Nathaniel Brown struck from a central position just outside of the area, stroking the ball into the bottom corner past Marvin Schwäbe to level proceedings heading into the interval.

After colliding with Cologne’s Tom Krauß in the first half, Olise remained in the dressing room at the break, with Kompany awarding Tim Binder his Bundesliga debut, as their injuries continued to mount up with Serge Gnabry and Luis Díaz already sidelined.

Shortly after the break, Moore came close to adding to his tally but was denied by Urbig from close range before Lennart Karl, who had been quiet in the first period, fired just wide minutes later. Urbig was called into action again, first to deny Said El Mala after a dizzying-run from Moore on the hour mark, before Linton Maina’s well struck follow-up volley stung the palms of the Bayern stopper – who is yet to keep a clean sheet this season.

In a recent development, both teams had chances to win it in the dying embers. Jamal Musiala, returning from injury, placed the ball just the wrong side of the post after superb play from Josip Stanišić and Karl before El Mala placed his shot from close-range agonisingly wide at the other end following Sebastian Sebulonsen’s cross.

The result keeps Bayern top of the Bundesliga, but Borussia Dortmund can climb above the leaders with a win against Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday, while Cologne remain winless in five Bundesliga games.

Bayern Munich: Urbig (7) – Laimer (5), Upamecano (6), Tah (6), Stanišić (5) – Kimmich (6), Pavlović (5), Karl (5), Olise (5), Brown (6) – Kane (-).

Others: Bischof (7), Binder (5), Musiala (-), Kim (-), Codjo-Evora (-).

According to recent reports, cologne: Schwäbe (6) – Simpson-Pusey (6), Schmied (5), Lochoshvili (6) – Sebulonsen (6), Okon-Engstler (6), Krauß (7), Sosa (6), Maina (6), Moore (7) – S. El Mala (6).

Others: Thielmann (-), Jóhannesson (-), Heskey (), Castro-Montes (), Bülter ().

The Englishman opened his Bundesliga account for the season with an outstanding, composed finish past Jonas Urbig. Showing clear development at Cologne, the 19-year-old almost added a second shortly after the break, but wasn’t able to generate enough power on his effort from close range, which was collected by Bayern’s custodian.

England's Euro 2028 mission starts NOW! Thomas Tuchel's men must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - or risk their 'DNA' cursing them yet again, writes OLIVER HOLT

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1326 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.
  • That is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 16:10 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 14 November 2026.

It is four months, almost to the day, since England shrank from the call of history and lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina in Atlanta but Thomas Tuchel may not believe that the Nations League tie against Spain in the Metropolitano on Sunday evening represents his best shot at redemption for the way things played out that afternoon in America’s South.

That is largely because Tuchel does not appear to believe he has anything to redeem himself for. The manner of his side’s capitulation - and the substitutions he made - in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium last July enraged the nation, but Tuchel mentioned the fault was in the damned DNA of the English, that we were underlings, and that our players found it constitutionally impossible to keep hold of the ball.

Whatever Tuchel thinks, the fact remains that the tie against Lamine Yamal, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Mikel Oyarzabal and the rest of the world champions at the home of Atletico Madrid offers Tuchel and his players the opportunity to encourage themselves and their fans that they are not destined to be also-rans wired to fall at the final hurdle for evermore.

Industry observers note that spain are formidable opposition. They are on a record-breaking run of 43 matches unbeaten and have won their last 12 in succession. They haven't drawn a game since their June 15 game against Cape Verde in the World Cup. Their last defeat was on March 22, 2024, when they lost 1-0 to Colombia in a friendly. Some ask whether they are the best international side the world has ever seen.

‘Spain seem unbeatable,’ Tuchel said, when he walked into the press room at the Metropolitano on Saturday night and heard hymns of praise being lavished upon the opponents he is about to face.

Industry observers note that ‘They have a very strong identity and a very strong mentality. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are up for the fight. We are up for a spectacular match. We can see how far we can push the limits with the world champions in Madrid. The group is full of self-belief and rightly so.’.

England must beat Spain to prove they can compete with the best - even if they have flaws.

Thomas Tuchel must show he can find a way around the limitations presented by the 'DNA' he has complained about.

In a recent development, this may be the toughest game that Tuchel’s England side play until the European Championships in 2028, where the final will be contested at Wembley, and they will play all their games at home. They need to go into that tournament with the belief that they can beat the best when the pressure is at its highest.

Beating Spain away in the final game of the group phase of the Nations League is not quite the same as a critical match at a major tournament but it is as stiff a challenge as Tuchel is going to face until then. Beating Croatia 7-0 in front of gangs of schoolkids in Rijeka last month was hailed as the best England performance of the Tuchel era. Which claims it all, really.

Sources indicate that it was a great performance in a relatively meaningless match. Now it is time for him to show that he can marshal an England side to succeed against the very best, not fall apart when the prize is in sight. His protestations of powerlessness in the aftermath of the Argentina defeat were not a good look for a coach who was hired with the idea that his coaching prowess and his game management could get England over the line.

Has he learned anything from the manner of the Argentina defeat? ‘This game against Spain will be proof of concept at the highest level,’ he said, ‘but we are up for it. I think we have taken the next step after the World Cup. The best thing is to trust our process and trust ourselves. We need to be clear about how we want to impose ourselves and I think that is all visible.’.

Now it is time for him to show that he can find a way past the limitations of England’s footballing DNA, find a way to compete with Spain and France when it really matters, and find a way to end the culture of near misses that has come to be England’s lot in the last decade of appearances in semi-finals and finals.

England have played six matches since that day of crushing disappointment in Atlanta and scored 22 goals. But in the only one of those matches that really mattered, they lost 3-2 to Spain at Wembley in the opening tie of their Nations League campaign at the end of September, a game in which they were largely outclassed by Luis de la Fuente’s team.

Industry observers note that spain are what England have to aim for. Tuchel mentioned their example and their ability and their mindset straight after the semi-final loss to Argentina. ‘Ball possession plays a crucial role,’ he said at his post-match press conference in Atlanta. ‘It’s maybe not in our DNA like it is in our Spanish DNA or in our Argentinian-Brazilian DNA, to take the ball and control the game with the ball.’.

This may well be their toughest game until the final of the 2028 European Championships, if they get that far.

It has been revealed that the England coach said more recently that England need to go back to trusting a traditional style that emphasises direct, high-intensity physicality rather than trying to copy Spanish patience in ball-retention. England, though, were taught a lesson in sophistication by the Spanish in September.

And for all the attention lavished on Yamal, Spain’s defence is the best in the world. Rodri, the shield for that defence and also the world’s best in the role, is not fit for this game but even without him, Spain’s back-line inspires an awful lot more confidence than England’s.

‘They were the best in the World Cup at the back,’ Declan Rice, England’s central midfielder, said on Saturday. ‘Defence wins you titles. Everyone talks about their attacking talent but you look at their central defenders, their full backs and the way their midfielders contribute to the defence, too.’.

That defence will have to stop England’s resurgent front line, led by Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who could be flanked by Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers and backed up by the supreme talent of Jude Bellingham just behind them.

According to recent reports, bellingham’s improving relationship with Tuchel, which cannot have been harmed by the inclusion of Bellingham’s brother, Jobe, in this squad, is another reason to hope that England still retain the capacity to improve after the World Cup. The elder Bellingham has become England’s most influential player.

Recent findings suggest that england at their best would be one of the few teams capable of extending them. Rice remarked on Saturday that the game between the two sides was ‘massive’. England need to prove they can find a way to get closer to the world champions. To beat them, Rice said, would be a ‘massive statement’.

‘Playing against them is a great incentive to win. It will show where we are as a group. We are trying to attack teams full throttle and with players like Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers in our attack, it feels as if it is going to take off one night and maybe tomorrow night will be the night. We can beat Spain. For sure, we can.’.

Sources indicate that tuchel needs to prove England can win, not just be noble contenders. They need to prove that their DNA need not be a curse.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.
  • On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) unveiled Keith Cooper had died aged 78.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:01 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 20:45 EST, 14 November 2026.

A former Premier League referee was mistakenly declared dead by football chiefs this week.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) unveiled Keith Cooper had died aged 78. But he is alive and well.

The news reached the ears of the Wembley Cup final referee when he went out to his local sports centre for a flu jab only to be told: 'You were dead.'.

The Football Association of Wales posted a statement online and a tribute on social media to announce his death, but then withdrew it within an hour.

Mr Cooper, who is the father of former Nottingham Forest and Leicester boss Steve Cooper, told a Welsh sports website: 'I walked into the sports centre yesterday to have my jab and the fellow went, "You were dead!".

'Well, I'm not dead, I'm here and I'm OK!'.

The blunder appears to have emerged after the Wiltshire FA announced the death of another referee called Keith Cooper, who the football chiefs in Wales believed was the other Keith Cooper.

The FAW statement said: 'Keith was a well-known figure who enjoyed an exceptional career at both domestic and international level and would later hold the position of FAW Referees' Officer following his retirement in 1996.

On Tuesday, the Football Association of Wales (FAW) unveiled Keith Cooper had died aged 78.

Mark Beeney goalkeeper of Leeds United is Sent Off of by Referee Keith A Cooper for hand ball outside the area during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Leeds United at Old Trafford on April 17, 1996 in Manchester, England.

Recent findings suggest that former professional football John Fashanu is pictured with referee Keith Cooper during a Wimbledon F.C. match.

'Born and raised in Pontypridd, he is considered one of Wales' best match officials through his highly-regarded status in the game.

'In addition to his work with FAW, Keith was also a valued member of the Wiltshire FA Council who recognised his 'integrity, passion and commitment' in their tribute to his services to the game.

'Everyone at the FAW sends their condolences to his family and friends at this sad time.'.

Mr Cooper oversaw the 1994 League Cup final between Aston Villa and Manchester United, won by Villa 3-1, and worked in radio punditry after hanging up his whistle.

It has been revealed that the FAW has not issued an explanation over the posted tribute. His family has not yet commented on the error.

But the unfortunate mistake has not spared the FAW from ridicule by other football fans.

One noted: 'We always said there was only one Keith Cooper - turns out there are two.'.

Another remarked: 'Glad the whistle wasn't blown too early on Keith and much respect to the family of the other one.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zabatta: “Verso gli Stati Generali dello Sport, una grande festa per tutta la Campania”.

Presentata in Consiglio regionale l’iniziativa del 22 novembre alla Mostra d’Oltremare. Una giornata ad ingresso libero tra campioni, scuole, associazioni e cittadini.

Recent findings suggest that una giornata per riunire il movimento sportivo campano, valorizzarne i protagonisti e promuovere una pratica sportiva sempre più accessibile e inclusiva. È “Verso gli Stati Generali dello Sport 2026”, l’iniziativa promossa dall’Assessorato allo Sport della Regione Campania, presentata questa mattina nella Sala Caduti di Nassiriya del Consiglio regionale.

L’appuntamento è per domenica 22 novembre alla Mostra d’Oltremare, Padiglione 3B , con incontri, premiazioni, attività dimostrative e occasioni di confronto tra istituzioni, federazioni, associazioni, scuole, atleti e cittadini.

Alla conferenza stampa hanno partecipato l’assessora regionale allo Sport Fiorella Zabatta, il presidente del Consiglio regionale Massimiliano Manfredi, Sandro Cuomo, campione olimpico nella spada a squadre ad Atlanta 1996, e l’atleta paralimpica Angela Procida.

Sources indicate that “Vogliamo che sia una grande festa dello sport campano, un’occasione per dare spazio a ogni disciplina, a ogni talento e a ogni storia. Lo sport è passione, sacrificio e inclusione, una palestra di vita che unisce generazioni e crea comunità. Con questa iniziativa, unica nel suo genere in Campania, vogliamo riunire chi vive lo sport ogni giorno: dagli atleti alle associazioni, dalle scuole alle federazioni, fino alle famiglie. Il nostro obiettivo è costruire uno sport davvero accessibile, perché non deve essere un privilegio legato alle possibilità economiche, ma un diritto e un’opportunità per tutti”, ha detto l’ assessora regionale allo Sport Fiorella Zabatta.

Recent findings suggest that ”Gli Stati generali dello sport devono segnare l’avvio di una nuova stagione di impegno e di politiche concrete per la Campania. Lo sport non è un lusso né un privilegio, ma un diritto e un fondamentale strumento di crescita, salute, educazione e inclusione sociale. La nostra sfida è garantire a ogni cittadino, indipendentemente dal territorio in cui vive o dalle proprie condizioni economiche e personali, la possibilità di praticarlo. Servono investimenti negli impianti, sostegno alle associazioni e alle società sportive e una particolare attenzione ai giovani, alle persone con disabilità e alle fasce più fragili. Il Consiglio regionale è pronto a fare la propria parte: dobbiamo trasformare le tante energie del mondo sportivo in una visione comune e in azioni concrete. Perché investire nello sport significa investire nel futuro, nella coesione e nella qualità della vita della nostra comunità. La Campania ha bisogno di una politica dello sport che non lasci indietro nessuno”, ha aggiunto il presidente del Consiglio regionale Massimiliano Manfredi.

Il programma del 22 novembre inizia alle 9.30 von l’accoglienza dei partecipanti; alle 10.30 apriranno gli stand delle Federazioni sportive campane. Alle 11 il convegno “Sport e scuola: educazione, inclusione e benessere” darà il via alla sessione mattutina, che proseguirà con le premiazioni di “Napoli Capitale Europea dello Sport” e i riconoscimenti alle scuole, alle associazioni e alle realtà che si sono distinte nella promozione della pratica sportiva.

Alle 18 si terrà il convegno “Presente e Futuro dello Sport in Campania”, seguito dalle premiazioni della Presidenza del Consiglio regionale e dai riconoscimenti ai grandi protagonisti dello sport, tra cui la campionessa olimpica di ginnastica artistica Manila Esposito, altri atleti e rappresentanti delle Federazioni sportive.

In a recent development, per tutta la giornata sarà possibile visitare gli stand, conoscere e provare diverse discipline sportive e partecipare alle attività dimostrative. Alle 20 è previsto lo show cooking “La dieta dello sportivo”.

Industry observers note that L’iniziativa è organizzata dall’Assessorato allo Sport della Regione Campania, con la partecipazione del CONI Campania, del Comitato Italiano Paralimpico (CIP), di Sport e Salute e di Padelness e Sport, con il supporto operativo di Sviluppo Campania. L’ingresso è libero .

  • Aurelio De Laurentiis ha definito l’accordo per l’acquisto dei terreni dove sorgerà il nuovo centro sportivo.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Aurelio De Laurentiis ha definito l’accordo per l’acquisto dei terreni dove sorgerà il nuovo centro sportivo. L’appuntamento sarebbe stato fissato mercoledì 18 novembre alle ore 12 nello studio notarile a Chiaia in via dei Mille di Francesco Coppa. Si tratta di un acquisto preliminare, che riguarderebbe suoli per 13 ettari, anche se in futuro nell’affare potrebbero rientrare almeno altri cinque ettari di terreni. Con le firme sui contratti, il presidente e la societ diventeranno ufficialmente proprietari di quasi 13 ettari in località Pozzo Nuovo a Qualiano. Le trattative sono terminate, entro gennaio 2027 inizieranno anche i lavori per la trasformazione dell’area. Il nuovo training center potrebbe essere operativo entro 12 mesi. Perché ora il Napoli ha fretta di spostarsi nella sua nuova casa: e quindi, verrà data la priorità alla realizzazione di (almeno) tre campi di calcio necessari per gli allenamenti della prima squadra, gli spogliatoi, le palestre, le piscine, le aree dei massaggi e quelle per gli uffici. E di una palazzina per il ristoro. Poi, solo in un secondo momento, si aprirà il cantiere per la foresteria e per la realizzazione di un convitto per i giovani. Lo scrive Il Corriere del Mezzogiorno.

Lazio, forza del gruppo, Dele-Bashiru: "Quest'anno siamo molto più uniti"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Laziopress

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il centrocampista parla del buon avvio di stagione e del clima nel gruppo.
  • Fisayo Dele-Bashiru è stato intervistato ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel al rientro dagli impegni con la Nazionale, in vista della sfida di sabato tra Lazio e Lecce.
  • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista parla del buon avvio di stagione e del clima nel gruppo.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru è stato intervistato ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel al rientro dagli impegni con la Nazionale, in vista della sfida di sabato tra Lazio e Lecce. Nel confronto racconta l'energia portata da Gattuso, la concorrenza interna e la voglia di dare il massimo per la squadra.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that sto bene. Sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. Naturalmente, essere convocato in Nazionale è sempre un momento speciale, soprattutto in occasione delle qualificazioni alla Coppa d'Africa. Le partite sono andate abbastanza bene. La prima è stata positiva, la seconda poteva andare meglio, ma sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. Nel fine settimana ci aspetta una partita importante e non vediamo l'ora di giocarla.

Sources indicate that penso che quest'anno abbiamo iniziato molto bene con Gattuso. Ha portato nuova energia nello spogliatoio e credo che questo si veda nei rapporti tra i compagni, nel nostro rapporto con l'allenatore e anche in quello con i tifosi. Se riusciremo a continuare su questa strada, sarà perfetto.

Tanto, in questo momento c'è molta concorrenza. Quando ho l'opportunità di entrare in campo per aiutare la squadra, cerco sempre di dare il massimo. Se dovessi giocare nel fine settimana, darò come sempre tutto me stesso. Credo che questo sia importante perché, per arrivare lontano in campionato, non bisogna poter contare soltanto sugli undici titolari: anche i giocatori in panchina devono dare il proprio contributo. È fondamentale.

Industry observers note that credo che la concorrenza sia sicuramente positiva e faccia bene. Tutte le migliori squadre del mondo hanno molta competizione interna e penso che questo permetta alla squadra di esprimere al meglio. In questo momento l'atmosfera è molto buona. Credo che nello spogliatoio ci siano molte più battute e momenti di leggerezza rispetto alla scorsa stagione, quando la situazione era differente. Quest'anno siamo molto più uniti e questo contribuisce sicuramente a creare un bel clima all'interno del gruppo.

Da quando sono alla Lazio ho avuto diversi allenatori. Credo che quest'anno un aspetto importante sia il grande coinvolgimento di Gattuso nel lavoro con il gruppo e con ogni singolo giocatore. Ha un ottimo rapporto con tutti i componenti della squadra e penso che questo sia fondamentale. Inoltre, sa perfettamente cosa significhi essere in campo ai massimi livelli, avendo avuto una grande carriera da calciatore. È un allenatore di altissimo livello, tutti i ragazzi gli vogliono bene e dobbiamo continuare a ottenere risultati per lui.

A livello personale sono una persona piuttosto tranquilla. Non lascio che quello che succede all'esterno influenzi troppo il mio modo di essere. Penso di comportarmi in campo proprio come nella vita di tutti i giorni: sono abbastanza rilassato e calmo, anche se so essere aggressivo quando serve. Direi che queste sono le caratteristiche che mi descrivono meglio.

A livello personale, il mio obiettivo è giocare il maggior numero possibile di partite e aiutare la squadra il più possibile, magari con gol e assist. Se riuscirò a fare tutto questo, penso che sarà una stagione davvero molto positiva, non soltanto per me, ma anche per tutti i ragazzi. Adesso dobbiamo semplicemente continuare a lavorare partita dopo partita. Speriamo di riuscire a proseguire su questa buona strada.

By WILKO MARTÍNEZ-CACHERO, US REPORTER.

Published: 20:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 21:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'.

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day.

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left).

According to recent reports, the DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'.

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but mentioned her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police stated the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships.

The family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS stated the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'.

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE noted the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'.

He added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'.

The Santoro twins were taken to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana after their arrest, WABE reported.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana.

The Lincoln Police Department signed an partnership agreement with ICE in July. A department officer arrested the brothers.

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, remarked he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez remarked the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'.

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.

Quello del futuro della porta dell'Inter resta un argomento caldo in casa nerazzurra. Perché Josep Martinez non ha ancora dato le giuste garanzie e perché in giro non mancano certo le occasioni. Come quella, riferita da Tuttosport, di Alisson, che a giugno si libererà gratis dal Liverpool:.

"Di certo, però, un’Inter che vorrà continuare a rimanere ad alti livelli in Italia e in Europa, non potrà affidarsi in futuro a un portiere che non dia garanzie granitiche. Provedel ha il physique du rôle per rimanere il secondo, ma Martinez per meritarsi la conferma da numero uno, dovrebbe disputare una seconda metà di annata se non da fenomeno, di certo senza sbavature. Il ruolo di portiere titolare per la stagione '27-28, è però già ora un argomento sul tavolo di Marotta e Baccin. Chiaramente Pepo non è ancora tagliato fuori dai giochi, ma è chiaro che il club stia facendo le sue riflessioni, anche perché da gennaio, ci sono dei profili sui quali si potrebbe già lavorare avendo i contratti in scadenza nel giugno 2027".

"Fra questi, c'è sicuramente Alisson Becker, ex Roma e da nove stagioni titolare del Liverpool. Il brasiliano ha l'accordo in scadenza fra sette mesi e potrebbe aver finito il suo ciclo con i Reds. Già la scorsa primavera Alisson era finito nei ragionamenti di alcuni club come Inter e poi Juventus. Per altro i nerazzurri avevano sfiorato il brasiliano già nel lontano 2009, quando a 17 anni si era messo in luce nelle giovanili della Selecao e dell'Internacional di Porto Alegre. Prima del passaggio al Perugia, Morresi è cresciuto nel settore giovanile della Treiese, dai Piccoli Amici ai Pulcini. L’arrivo alla Lazio nell’estate del 2025 ha aperto una nuova tappa del suo percorso: con la maglia biancoceleste ha trovato spazio stabilmente davanti alla difesa.

Fino alla domenica del derby, la Lazio condivideva con la Roma l’imbattibilità in campionato. Anche il lavoro di Morresi davanti alla retroguardia contribuisce all’equilibrio della squadra.

Dall’altra parte c’era il miglior attacco del girone, capace di mettere alla prova la mediana biancoceleste. La Roma ha prevalso per 3-1 dopo aver dominato gran parte degli 80 minuti, ma nella ripresa la Lazio ha trovato la forza di reagire.

Il giornalista Maurizio Cardone ha parlato a MilanNews.it della situazione del Milan, che si ritrova davanti a un momento cruciale della stagione: "La rosa è corta e incompleta, lo sappiamo. A questo si aggiungono gli infortuni di Chukwueze, Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek, Tomori, Terracciano. È chiaro che per l’allenatore avere scelte così limitate nei numeri e nelle caratteristiche è una difficoltà non di poco conto. Ma è anche per questo che chi va in campo, soprattutto chi gioca meno, deve dimostrare in ogni partita di essere da Milan prendendosi le dovute responsabilità".

In a recent development, continua e conclude Maurizio Cardone sul Milan: "Se analizziamo l’andamento in campionato, a questa squadra mancano solo i due punti col Sassuolo perché credo che nell’economia di una stagione, una caduta come quella col Bologna ci possa stare. Amorim sta facendo un buon lavoro e a volte riceve critiche eccessive. Gli va dato tempo di lavorare e plasmare la squadra secondo la sua idea di calcio, magari con due - tre innesti di qualità a gennaio. Intanto però l’obiettivo è chiaro: provare a viaggiare a marce alte sia in campionato che in Europa League. La settimana che abbiamo davanti ci dirà se il Milan avrà fatto questo step di maturità".

On The Road: Overpowered by County, but Accies are making small steps in the long road back from the abyss

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.
  • The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026.

Hamilton Academical 1 Ross County 2.

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

Sources indicate that county, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so Newly introduced Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County.

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

Sources indicate that ‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he mentioned. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’.

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

According to recent reports, ‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he stated. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’.

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he stated: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’.

According to recent reports, edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he said.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek.

With 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ said Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

Industry observers note that ‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’.

Sources indicate that the Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ stated McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ said McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’.

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’.

He added: ‘The latest guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’.

According to recent reports, there were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

In a recent development, ‘It’s about loyalty,’ he mentioned. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’.

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he stated. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’.

According to recent reports, A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he said. ‘This season we are going up.’.

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game.

Sources indicate that brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

It has been revealed that he was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

Industry observers note that ‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he remarked. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’.

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he noted.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County.

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he remarked. ‘We are scoring team goals.’.

Sources indicate that has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’.

It was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he said.

Recent findings suggest that he added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’.

It has been revealed that asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he remarked: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’.

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

Arsenal e Valencia: sei un esploratore del mondo. Che passaggi sono stati?
